## How I can help

- **Frontend Development**: Responsive interfaces in React, Next.js and TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS or Bootstrap. Layouts that hold together from a narrow phone to a wide desktop, without a separate mobile codebase.
- **Backend & APIs**: Node.js and Express services, Python and Django applications, and REST APIs designed to be consumed — including AI API integration where a product needs it.
- **Full-Stack Product Work**: End-to-end features across the stack: PostgreSQL and Prisma for data, Redux Toolkit for client state, JWT for secure user management — one coherent path from schema to screen.
- **Testing & QA**: Manual web testing, API testing in Postman and systematic debugging. Finding the defect before a user does is cheaper than every alternative.
- **Data & Reporting**: Data management and analysis with MS Excel and Power BI, plus validation checks that keep a data flow reliable across multiple sources.

# ConsentX — Pradeep Maurya

A consent management platform where privacy choices have to be captured, stored and proven.

Canonical: https://www.pradeepmaury.in/work/consentx.html

---

Contributed to full-stack development and ongoing enhancement of ConsentX.io — a consent management platform — covering responsive UI, user-facing functionality, testing and usability improvements.

Working on a live product, the brief was rarely "build this screen." It was closer to "this flow confuses people and the numbers show it." Most of my work sat in that gap: taking an existing interface, finding where it broke down on real viewports and real data, and rebuilding it so the consent journey reads clearly from first load to confirmation.

Beyond the frontend, I picked up backend tasks and application functionality, debugged issues reported from production, and tested each change manually and through the API before it shipped.

## Details

- Role: Full Stack Developer
- Context: iLeads Auxiliary Services (SS IntelligenceX)
- Year: 2026
- Stack: React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, REST APIs
- Scope: Website development, responsive UI, user-facing functionality, testing, usability
- Live: https://consentx.io

### Responsive first

Consent interfaces get opened on whatever device is nearest. Every layout was rebuilt to hold up from a narrow phone through to a wide desktop without a separate mobile path to maintain.

### Tested before shipped

Each change went through manual web testing plus API checks in Postman, so regressions were caught before review rather than after release.

---

# RegulatoryBridge — Pradeep Maurya

A regulatory compliance platform — dense information that still has to be quick to read.

Canonical: https://www.pradeepmaury.in/work/regulatorybridge.html

---

Contributed to website development and improvements for RegulatoryBridge.com, covering responsive design, feature refinement, debugging, testing and performance-focused updates.

Compliance products carry a lot of information per screen, which makes them easy to build badly. The work here was mostly about restraint: tightening layouts so dense tables and long-form requirements stay scannable, and refining existing features rather than stacking new ones on top.

Alongside that I handled debugging and testing passes, and performance-focused updates where pages were doing more work than the content justified.

## Details

- Role: Full Stack Developer
- Context: iLeads Auxiliary Services (SS IntelligenceX)
- Year: 2026
- Stack: React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, REST APIs
- Scope: Website development, responsive design, feature refinement, debugging, testing, performance
- Live: https://regulatorybridge.com

### Refine over rebuild

Most tickets were improvements to shipped features. Changing a live product without disrupting the people already using it is its own constraint.

### Performance as a feature

On an information-dense platform, how fast a page becomes readable matters as much as what it says.

---

# Bakery — Pradeep Maurya

A complete bakery shop — storefront, cart and secure accounts, built end to end.

Canonical: https://www.pradeepmaury.in/work/bakery.html

---

Built a full-stack bakery shop application using Next.js, Express.js, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Redux Toolkit and JWT authentication, with secure user management and REST APIs.

This is the project where the whole stack was mine. Next.js on the front, Express and PostgreSQL behind it, Prisma handling the schema and queries, Redux Toolkit holding client state, and JWT for authentication — so every decision, from the data model up to the cart interaction, had to actually connect to the next one.

Building it end to end is what made the API boundary real. Designing the REST endpoints and then being the one to consume them teaches you quickly which responses are convenient and which only looked tidy on paper.

## Details

- Role: Full-stack developer (personal project)
- Context: Self-directed
- Year: 2025
- Stack: Next.js, Express.js, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Redux Toolkit, JWT
- Scope: Full-stack build: storefront, cart, secure user management, REST APIs

### Secure by default

JWT authentication with protected routes and server-side validation, so account and order data is never guarded by the UI alone.

### One schema, one source of truth

Prisma over PostgreSQL kept the data model explicit and migrations reviewable instead of improvised.

---

# Xamlysis — Pradeep Maurya

An online examination portal — the kind of app where a bug has a deadline attached.

Canonical: https://www.pradeepmaury.in/work/xamlysis.html

---

Worked on an online examination portal, supporting core features such as authentication and exam creation, alongside testing and stability improvements.

Exam software has an unusual failure cost: a defect does not merely annoy someone, it interrupts a timed assessment that cannot simply be retaken. That shaped how I worked on it — authentication and exam creation were built with the unhappy paths treated as first-class, not as edge cases to handle later.

A large share of my contribution was testing and stability: exercising flows the way a stressed user would, reproducing intermittent issues, and closing them properly rather than papering over the symptom.

## Details

- Role: Developer / QA support
- Context: Project work
- Year: 2025
- Stack: JavaScript, Node.js, REST APIs, manual & API testing
- Scope: Core features including authentication and exam creation, plus testing and stability work

### Auth before features

Role-correct access to exam creation and exam taking was the foundation everything else sat on.

### Stability as the deliverable

On a portal under time pressure, "it reliably works" is the feature users actually notice.

---

# Movie Scraper — Pradeep Maurya

A Django app that pulls movie data from several sources and refuses to trust any of them.

Canonical: https://www.pradeepmaury.in/work/movie-scraper.html

---

Developed a Django-based application with data validation and checks to support reliable data flow from multiple sources.

Scraping is the easy half. The moment data arrives from more than one source, the interesting problem becomes disagreement: missing fields, different formats for the same value, and records that are confidently wrong. The application is built around that — validation and checks sit between collection and storage, so bad records are caught at the boundary.

Working on it changed how I think about ingestion generally. A pipeline without validation is not a pipeline, it is a way to move someone else's errors into your own database.

## Details

- Role: Developer
- Context: Self-directed
- Year: 2025
- Stack: Python, Django, data validation
- Scope: Django application with validation and checks for reliable multi-source data flow

### Validate at the boundary

Checks run before anything is stored, which keeps the database trustworthy instead of requiring cleanup passes later.

### Multiple sources, one shape

Normalising differing source formats into a single schema is what makes the collected data actually usable.

# Privacy — Pradeep Maurya

Privacy for Pradeep Maurya's portfolio.

Canonical: https://www.pradeepmaury.in/privacy.html

---

This site is a personal portfolio. It does not run analytics, advertising or third-party trackers, and it sets no cookies.

## What is collected

Nothing automatically. If you use the contact form, the details you type — name, email, optional company and your message — are used solely to reply to you.

## How the contact form works

Unless a form endpoint is configured, the form opens your own email client with the message pre-filled. In that case nothing is transmitted to this site at all; you send the email yourself.

## Fonts and assets

All fonts, scripts and images are served from this site. No requests are made to external services while you browse.

## Contact

Questions about this note: pradeepmaurya2002@gmail.com.
